newsitem.title: USA: Elizabeth Dole goes back to work at Red Cross.
newsitem.headline: Elizabeth Dole goes back to work at Red Cross.

text.p: Elizabeth Dole, wife of losing presidential candidate Bob Dole, returned to work Thursday as president of the American Red Cross while her husband kept up weighing job possibilities.

Mrs. Dole, 60, who took a leave of absence from America's largest charity in November 1995 to help her husband's third bid for the White House, walked into her office at 8 a.m., said Red Cross spokesman Roy Clason.

While her husband considers non-government work after losing to President Clinton on Nov. 5, Mrs. Dole -- sometimes mentioned as a potential Republican presidential candidate herself -- has a full agenda ahead.

She is the equivalent of a chief executive officer of a major corporation. The Red Cross annual budget of $1.8 billion a year is more than budgets of half of the big companies listed among the Fortune 500 firms, noted spokesman Clason.
Her annual salary is $200,000. She decided to take no salary in her first year on the job in 1991 and since then has accepted salary but also donated to the Red Cross $494,000, said Clason.
As president of the non-profit group, she will be in charge of 1.4 million volunteers and 31,000 paid employees.

"Coming back to the Red Cross is like coming home," Mrs. Dole said in a statement. "I am delighted to be rejoining the dedicated volunteers and staff who help this wonderful organisation do so much good for so many people. For me, the Red Cross is a mission field, and it's great to be back."
In praising her return, Red Cross Chairman Norman Augustine said "I can think of no finer way to begin 1997."

Before joining the Red Cross, Mrs. Dole had a lengthy career in Washington politics but had never sought office. She had served in the White House, was a member of the Federal Trade Commission, transportation secretary under then President Ronald Reagan and labour secretary under former President George Bush.

Mrs. Dole, whose office is a stone's throw from the White House she and her husband would have occupied had he won, is the first woman to head the Red Cross since Clara Barton founded and headed the organisation in 1881.

Meantime her husband has kept active since losing the election, making late night guest appearances on NBC's "The Tonight Show with Jay Leno," CBS's "Late Show with David Letterman" and NBC's "Saturday Night Live."

Bob Dole, 73, appears Jan. 9 in a short TV segment on NBC's situation comedy "Suddenly Susan" starring Brooke Shields, in an episode giving tips on how government works to a character on the show trying to become a U.S. citizen.

"There's nothing left to do but go out and get rich," Dole told Jay Leno on his Dec. 16 show, when asked what he planned to do. Dole spent 35 years in Washington as a House member and senator before quitting Congress to campaign last summer.
The former candidate has been going into his old campaign office in Washington almost daily.

He writes letters and thanks supporters, said spokesman Clarkson Hine, and considers job prospects with law firms and possible speaking engagements. Dole, who has a withered right arm from combat wounds in World War II, also has said he plans to work to help fellow disabled people.
